contract: Play Matroska, MOV/MP4, TS188 and M2TS192 through Player and the PGS, DVD and DVB subtitle bridges. The pinned FFmpeg subtitles build demuxes the same track and calls avcodec_decode_subtitle2. The plain link serves future measurement.

Fold each published bitmap event, its presentation clock, rectangle count, geometry, forced flag, every declared ARGB palette entry and every visible index row. DVD also compares start and end display offsets. The DVB queue exposes its presentation clock without a display duration; Matroska block DTS is absent at the source boundary, so the reference's inferred DTS is diagnostic only.

Matroska PGS startup cases also fold the startup clock projection, packet duration and codec bytes for every selected packet, against the demuxer's packet view. Include single-service DVB files and explicit service-selection cases for both descriptor arrangements. Alternate decoder-only configuration modes are covered by the standalone subtitle contracts.
Preload the container on both sides. Opening and reading the container, decoding, folding and teardown are inside the operation.

pending_module_requirements: The DVB queue exposes at most eight regions. The reference decoder returns the full region list.
The DVB queue uses zero when the decode event has no clock. The reference AVSubtitle preserves the unknown clock.
The selected page and its ancillary pages come from the PMT descriptor. The reference's stream-wide service and page selection publishes a different display set or clear.
The player's strict subtitle PES path does not publish this length-zero private stream packet. The reference demuxer recovers its DVB segment payload.
The source player uses an explicit epoch-zero 33-bit clock. The reference demuxer reports a signed continuation across the MPEG-TS wrap.
The bridge binds to a strict, explicitly signalled DVB service and default construction requires one service. The reference demuxer can infer, merge or replace descriptor information.
The Matroska VobSub bridge requires track initialization. The reference decoder supplies default palette and canvas values when it receives an unconfigured packet.
The bridge retains the MP4 sample-table clock. The reference decoder receives the demuxer's edit-list timeline.
Matroska block times and inferred durations reach the candidate's bounded startup or source projection. FFmpeg rounds, anchors or leaves these laced clocks unknown along its own demux path.
